label: H.R. 10375

summary: H.R. 10375, the 504 Modernization and Small Manufacturer Enhancement Act of 2026, amends the Small Business Investment Act of 1958 and the Small Business Act to modify the Small Business Administration's 504 loan guaranty program. The bill adds new policy goals related to workforce development, disaster recovery areas, and very small businesses; streamlines loan closing procedures for certain lenders and attorneys; sets new marketing and outreach requirements; updates building occupancy and leasing rules for new facilities and existing buildings; and alters credit exemption rules.

affected_groups.effect: Gain expanded access to affordable capital, altered occupancy and leasing rules for facilities, and added paths to meet loan policy goals through workforce training.
Receive new authorities to handle administrative loan-closing tasks, conduct regular examinations for specific existing building leases, and file anti-investor certifications.
affected_groups.group: Certified Development Companies and Accredited Lenders

affected_groups.effect: Tasked with establishing marketing plans, conducting file reviews through the Office of Credit Risk Management, altering district counsel review responsibilities, and submitting a congressional impact report after 5 years.
affected_groups.group: Small Business Administration (SBA) and District Counsels

key_provisions: Adds new development company program policy goals for workforce development training programs, revitalizing disaster-declared areas, and expanding small businesses with 10 or fewer employees.

Allows accredited lender certified companies to take specific administrative actions to facilitate loan closings, such as reallocating project costs up to 10 percent, making typographical corrections, and adjusting borrower or guarantor roles.
Shifts file review responsibilities for loans closed by designated attorneys to the Office of Credit Risk Management and removes related closing package review duties from SBA district counsels.
Directs the SBA Administrator to develop and implement a marketing and outreach plan regarding the availability of loans within one year of enactment.
Updates leasing and occupancy rules for new facilities, allowing small manufacturers to permanently occupy and use 50 percent of a project rather than the standard 60 percent.

Establishes leasing rules for existing buildings, including specific occupancy thresholds, maximum lease terms of 1 year for residential leases and 5 years for commercial leases, and annual or biennial compliance exams.
missing_information: Specific funding amounts or appropriations authorized to carry out the marketing and outreach plan.
Detailed metrics or criteria the SBA will use to evaluate the 5-year impact report.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 10375, the 504 Modernization and Small Manufacturer Enhancement Act of 2026, amends the Small Business Investment Act of 1958 and the Small Business Act to modify the Small Business Administration's 504 loan guaranty program. The bill adds new policy goals related to workforce development, disaster recovery areas, and very small businesses; streamlines loan closing procedures for certain lenders and attorneys; sets new marketing and outreach requirements; updates building occupancy and leasing rules for new facilities and existing buildings; and alters credit exemption rules.
summary_detail.significance: The bill updates the operational rules, administrative procedures, and policy priorities of the federal 504 loan guaranty program for small businesses and small manufacturers.
